skill.name: agentic-browser
skill.description: Browser automation for AI agents through inference.sh sessions. It opens pages, interacts with element references, captures screenshots, and runs page JavaScript.
skill.summary: Automate browser navigation, interaction, screenshots, and page inspection through inference.sh.
skill.author: inference-sh

security_audit.summary: The reviewed skill is primarily documentation for controlling an inference.sh browser session. Most static findings are false positives from markdown code fences and inline backticks, but the quick-start command that pipes a remote installer into sh is a confirmed critical supply-chain risk.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipe-to-shell command with a package manager install, checksum verification, or a signed release download before execution.

remediation.issue: The installer URL is hardcoded in the quick-start command.
remediation.suggestion: Document the trusted source, expected checksum, and manual verification steps for the installer before users run it.

remediation.issue: Browser automation can execute page JavaScript and submit forms.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to use the skill only on authorized sites and to avoid entering secrets unless the site and session are trusted.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Workflows with Agentic Browser
content.value_statement: Manual browser tasks slow research, testing, and data collection. This skill lets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code operate a browser through inference.sh sessions.
actual_capabilities: Opens URLs in an inference.sh browser session and returns page state.
Lists interactive elements with @e references for follow-up actions.
Clicks, fills, types, selects, hovers, scrolls, waits, and navigates back.
Captures page screenshots, including full-page screenshots.
Runs JavaScript in the current page for extraction or inspection.
Keeps browser state across calls until the session is closed.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, CLI access, and successful login.
Web pages can change, so element references may expire after updates.
Automation should only run on sites where the user has authorization.
JavaScript execution is limited to the active page and browser session.

use_cases.title: Test Web Form Flows
use_cases.description: Open a form, fill fields, click controls, and capture the resulting page state.

use_cases.title: Collect Research Evidence
use_cases.description: Navigate pages, inspect visible elements, and capture screenshots for review notes.

use_cases.title: Extract Website Data
use_cases.description: Use page snapshots and controlled JavaScript to collect repeated data from authorized sites.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agentic-browser to open this URL: [URL]. Report the page title, current URL, and main interactive elements.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Simple Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], identify the form fields, fill them with these values: [VALUES], then show the resulting page state.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate through this workflow on [URL]: [STEPS]. After each navigation, refresh the snapshot and note visible success or error states.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Page Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], inspect the page structure, run safe page JavaScript to collect [DATA], and summarize the extracted results.

output_examples.input: Open a product page and identify checkout controls.
output_examples.output: The page loaded successfully. I found product options, quantity controls, an add-to-cart button, and a checkout link.

output_examples.input: Capture the current page after submitting a contact form.
output_examples.output: The form was submitted. The new page state shows a confirmation message and no visible validation errors.

output_examples.input: Extract headings from a documentation page.
output_examples.output: The page contains setup, authentication, sessions, functions, examples, and troubleshooting sections.

best_practices: Start with a new session, then reuse the returned session ID for related actions.
Refresh the snapshot after navigation, form submission, or dynamic page updates.
Close browser sessions when the task is complete.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse element references after the page changes or navigates.
Do not automate sites where you lack permission to browse or submit data.
Do not place passwords or sensitive tokens into prompts unless the site is trusted.

faq.question: What does this skill control?
faq.answer: It controls an inference.sh browser session through open, snapshot, interact, screenshot, execute, and close functions.

faq.question: Does it require inference.sh?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow requires the inference.sh CLI, an account, and login before browser commands work.

faq.question: Can it click and fill forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It can click, fill, type, select, hover, scroll, press keys, wait, and go back.

faq.question: Can it run JavaScript?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run JavaScript in the active page for inspection or data extraction.

faq.question: When should I refresh the snapshot?
faq.answer: Refresh after navigation, form submission, dynamic loading, or any action that changes the page.

faq.question: Is the quick-start installer safe?
faq.answer: The report flags the pipe-to-shell installer as risky. Verify the installer source before running it.
